# Permanent gate failure-diagnosis ledger

## Operative role

<issue id="a99e9032-3a9e-4189-b7f5-df88a9c6e4d7" href="https://linear.app/harneet2512/issue/HAR-55/permanent-gate-failure-diagnosis-ledger">HAR-55</issue> is the append-only failure-class registry. It records diagnoses and closures but grants no construction or review authority. Every worker reads <issue id="2df733cf-4e19-4788-812f-52281ac0c5db" href="https://linear.app/harneet2512/issue/HAR-58/final-stand">HAR-58</issue> first; <issue id="2df733cf-4e19-4788-812f-52281ac0c5db" href="https://linear.app/harneet2512/issue/HAR-58/final-stand">HAR-58</issue> alone defines product order and the approval stop. <issue id="6f7d9dd6-d186-4cb2-93a7-eb7a37d9e2f6" href="https://linear.app/harneet2512/issue/HAR-56/gt-pipelined-commit-queue-of-record">HAR-56</issue> records construction boundaries and <issue id="ecb76e90-9d07-40b8-b0dd-c97d74899dc4" href="https://linear.app/harneet2512/issue/HAR-57/gt-pipelined-deep-review-record">HAR-57</issue> records exact-SHA reviews.

## Identity invariant

* Every newly defined failure class receives the next globally unused `FD-NNN` identifier.
* An identifier belongs to one canonical defect definition. Later attempts, recurrences, and closures reference that identifier rather than defining it again.
* Narrative headings below predate this invariant and are immutable history. The executable duplicate-ID validator checks the canonical registry/new definitions and reports legacy ambiguity separately; it must fail closed for any new duplicate definition.
* `FD-029` is reserved for its pre-existing historical defect. The recurring RED-output reproducibility class is `FD-030`.

## Required entry schema

Every new definition contains the stable ID, failed gate and exact artifact, defect class, file/symbol evidence, decisive observed fixture, recurrence/attempt links, disposition, and exact review/repair SHAs when known.

## Control invariant

Failures are recorded here before their repair is selected. Selection comes only from the current <issue id="2df733cf-4e19-4788-812f-52281ac0c5db" href="https://linear.app/harneet2512/issue/HAR-58/final-stand">HAR-58</issue> product pipeline. <issue id="86d56678-c8ae-480d-a918-dc9ce2c320d2" href="https://linear.app/harneet2512/issue/HAR-34/live-chat-codex-and-reviewer-control-thread">HAR-34</issue> and PLAN-001 are retired and non-authoritative. A repeated mechanism is repaired structurally; it is not relabeled or patched one receipt at a time.

## Historical entries

## Backfilled entries from tonight

### FD-001 - confidence threshold creates source authority

* Gate: original R26 byte review, transferred through HAR-47 and authorized in HAR-34 R34.
* Class: `AUTHORITY_COLLAPSE`; related family: `FABRICATED_EVIDENCE`.
* Finding: `ResolveWithProvenance` allowed confidence thresholds to establish `source_supported` and selection rather than a closed provenance rule.
* Evidence: resolver authority/selection symbols in the 22-file R26 artifact.
* Decisive fixture: a candidate with high numeric confidence but no allowed source provenance must remain candidate-only and unselected.
* Disposition: repaired in `4fe4de5af7d4b838794eac413edb6e3d7337dca5`; independently accepted at R38.

### FD-002 - invented candidate confidence persisted as fixed weights

* Gate: original R26 byte review.
* Class: `FABRICATED_EVIDENCE`.
* Finding: candidate edges persisted fixed 0.6/0.2 weights without labeled calibration, allowing invented numbers to masquerade as evidence.
* Evidence: resolver candidate weighting and store edge publication in the R26 artifact.
* Decisive fixture: candidate edges persist no uncalibrated confidence; ranking changes only through an identified versioned query policy and `derived_score` is not persisted.
* Recurrence family: same class as FD-009 and FD-010. All persist claims that the producer did not observe.
* Disposition: repaired in `4fe4de5af7d4b838794eac413edb6e3d7337dca5`; independently accepted at R38.

### FD-003 - open ReceiverOrigin vocabulary

* Gate: original R26 byte review.
* Class: `POLICY_DIVERGENCE`.
* Finding: receiver-origin values, including `type_qualifier`, were not closed and versioned, so producer and consumer interpretations could diverge.
* Evidence: resolver validation and resolution contract types in the R26 artifact.
* Decisive fixture: every allowed value validates and every unknown value fails closed or follows an explicit typed path.
* Disposition: repaired in `4fe4de5af7d4b838794eac413edb6e3d7337dca5`; independently accepted at R38.

### FD-004 - incomplete graph/build identity binding

* Gate: original R26 byte review.
* Class: `IDENTITY_BINDING`.
* Finding: graph completion metadata was not atomically bound to full producer identity, executable/source fingerprint, repository revision, toolchain/tags, and receipt.
* Evidence: `cmd/gt-index/build_info.go`, `cmd/gt-index/main.go`, and store publication in the R26 artifact.
* Decisive fixture: failed or stale publication cannot expose a complete graph; successful completion reads back one internally consistent identity tuple and receipt hash.
* Disposition: repaired in `4fe4de5af7d4b838794eac413edb6e3d7337dca5`; independently accepted at R38.

### FD-005 - candidate-first query hides unresolved callsites

* Gate: original R26 byte review.
* Class: `QUERY_OMISSION`.
* Finding: an inner candidate join omitted zero-candidate, dynamic, external-unresolved, and parser-incomplete callsites.
* Evidence: attached-candidate query in `internal/store/sqlite.go` in the R26 artifact.
* Decisive fixture: callsite-first revision-checked query returns each required unresolved state with zero candidates.
* Disposition: repaired in `4fe4de5af7d4b838794eac413edb6e3d7337dca5`; independently accepted at R38.

### FD-006 - dynamic-call policy inconsistent across layers

* Gate: original R26 byte review.
* Class: `POLICY_DIVERGENCE`.
* Finding: dynamic calls could be retained, dropped, or selected differently across parser, resolver, storage, query, docs, and tests.
* Evidence: dynamic dispatch paths across the R26 22-file artifact.
* Decisive fixture: dynamic callsite is always retained, with source-supported viable candidates but no unsafe selection when available, otherwise explicit typed zero-candidate abstention.
* Disposition: repaired in `4fe4de5af7d4b838794eac413edb6e3d7337dca5`; independently accepted at R38.

### FD-007 - structural authority leaks into target authority

* Gate: original R26 byte review.
* Class: `STRUCTURE_TARGET_COLLAPSE`.
* Finding: unresolved or candidate-only targets could inherit structural certification through `HAS_CALLSITE` or generic graph consumers.
* Evidence: graph edge authority and attached resolution publication in the R26 artifact.
* Decisive fixture: structural callsite certification never upgrades target-resolution authority; unresolved targets remain unresolved in primary consumers.
* Disposition: repaired in `4fe4de5af7d4b838794eac413edb6e3d7337dca5`; independently accepted at R38.

### FD-008 - selected target published twice as generic CALLS

* Gate: HAR-34 R38, exact SHA `4fe4de5af7d4b838794eac413edb6e3d7337dca5`.
* Class: `DUPLICATE_PUBLICATION`.
* Finding: legacy publication and `insertResolutionV2FactsTx` each inserted generic `CALLS` for the same source/target.
* Evidence: `cmd/gt-index/main.go` legacy edge publication; `internal/store/resolution_v2.go::insertResolutionV2FactsTx` v2 selection publication.
* Decisive fixture: one-call real CLI produced two CALLS rows before repair. After `76b02a446009d0260d14329348dbdc83f5a99f0d`, the same fixture produced one CALLS endpoint plus one distinct `SELECTED_TARGET`; migration coalescing and uniqueness rejection also passed.
* Disposition: verified closed at `76b02a446009d0260d14329348dbdc83f5a99f0d`.

### FD-009 - unexecuted passes fabricated as closed completeness

* Gate: HAR-34 R38, exact SHA `4fe4de5af7d4b838794eac413edb6e3d7337dca5`.
* Class: `FABRICATED_EVIDENCE`.
* Finding: `resolutionCoverage` defaulted non-winning passes to `completed_no_match`; v2 publication upgraded them to `closed` even after resolver early exit.
* Evidence: `internal/store/sqlite.go::resolutionCoverage`; `internal/store/resolution_v2.go::prepareResolutionV2`.
* Decisive fixture: real-CLI same-file early winner persisted later unexecuted passes as closed before repair.
* Recurrence: same class as FD-002. Invented candidate confidence claimed unsupported certainty; invented completeness claimed unsupported execution.
* Disposition: repair attempt `76b02a446009d0260d14329348dbdc83f5a99f0d` fixed the early-winner output but failed the full invariant; recurrence FD-010.

### FD-010 - completeness recurs as winner-only inference

* Gate: HAR-34 R40, exact SHA `76b02a446009d0260d14329348dbdc83f5a99f0d`.
* Class: `FABRICATED_EVIDENCE`.
* Finding: `resolutionPassExecutions(call, rc)` runs after `resolveInternal` returns and reconstructs history from final `rc.Method`. It has no branch that emits `completed_no_match`; every non-winner becomes `not_run/no_execution_event`.
* Evidence: `internal/resolver/resolver.go::resolveInternal`, `ResolveWithProvenance`, and `resolutionPassExecutions`.
* Decisive fixture: exact-SHA real-CLI import case. Same-file/lexical lookup executed and missed, import lookup won, yet persisted coverage was lexical `not_run/no_execution_event`, import `completed_match`, later passes `not_run`; graph facts were direct binding `not_run` and import binding `closed`.
* Recurrence: second failure of FD-009 and same fabricated-evidence family as FD-002. The first implementation fabricated a full closed vector; the second fabricated a winner-only vector. This triggers the rule that the structural gate/spec must change rather than repeating the same implementation request.
* Disposition: escalated and structurally respecified in HAR-30/HAR-42: no after-the-fact reporters, every state value needs a producing branch and fixture, observability fixtures are RED-first and include the negative path. HAR-34 R40 carries the current complete repair scope in the single control-description field.

## Entry discipline

Append only. Never rewrite an earlier diagnosis to make a later repair look successful. Closure is a later line with the exact repair SHA, independent fixture output, and reviewer verdict. If a defect reappears, create a new ID and link the earlier ID; do not silently reopen or overwrite it.

### FD-011 - R40 RED checkpoint missing before push

* Gate: first run of the gated single-ticket protocol, R40 repair from `76b02a446009d0260d14329348dbdc83f5a99f0d` to `4967e0080cef47f614b1761a3152b784c0355a30`.
* Class: `PROTOCOL_CHECKPOINT_OMISSION`.
* Finding: no durable RED-reproduced checkpoint reached the reviewer/main agent before the pushed SHA became visible. The available record moves from authorization/acknowledgement to pushed code without evidence that the later-pass fixture existed and failed before product implementation.
* Evidence: HAR-34 contains R40 scope and worker control acknowledgements but no construction receipt establishing the fixture-only RED state before commit; the remote advanced to `4967e008...` before a RED report was available.
* Decisive check: a pre-implementation fixture commit is not required, but the durable construction record must include the exact fixture, command, failing output, and timestamp before product-code mutation. That evidence is absent, so genuine RED-before-code cannot be established.
* Recurrence: none yet. This is our protocol failure, not a product-code defect and not evidence that the final code is wrong.
* Disposition: process correction required. Future units may not claim the entry gate passed without the durable RED checkpoint. The R40 code verdict separately follows exact-SHA rebuild and persisted-output review.

#### FD-011 disposition - explicit one-time waiver

User decision: accept the independently verified code PASS at `4967e0080cef47f614b1761a3152b784c0355a30` with a one-time waiver for the unprovable RED-before-code checkpoint. Do not manufacture a replay commit or invent missing history. The product fix is accepted; the process failure remains recorded and is enforced prospectively by the minimal fixture-first pre-push check. This waiver applies only to R40/FD-011 and creates no standing exception.

### FD-012 - launcher instruction overrides live-turn contract

* Gate: R41 continuation after worker acknowledgement C70/C71.
* Class: `UNENFORCED_CONTROL_CLAIM`, in the `FABRICATED_EVIDENCE` family.
* Finding: HAR-34 required the worker to remain in the same turn and continue authorized work, but the actual invocation was hard-prompted `CONTROL MODE ONLY`. The worker acknowledged R41 and then emitted C72 `CONTROL_ONLY_HANDOFF` without repository inspection, RED artifact, or construction.
* Evidence: HAR-34 header was synchronized at reviewer 41 / worker ACK 41 / authorization true; C72 states the invocation-level CONTROL restriction prevented R41 construction. Remote remained `4967e0080cef47f614b1761a3152b784c0355a30`.
* Defect mechanism: an invocation-level instruction outranked a ticket-level operating rule. A contract written only in Linear cannot enforce itself against a launcher that supplies a contradictory mode. This is the same family as fabricated evidence: the description claimed an automatic continuation behavior for which the active launcher provided no producing mechanism.
* Decisive fixture: launch a fresh construction-capable turn with no CONTROL-only restriction, acknowledged authorized R41 state, and the live-turn continuation rule in the invocation. It must create the RED checkpoint, construct, push, remain alive, poll for verdict, and continue without a human restart.
* Recurrence: follows FD-011 as a second protocol failure, but a distinct mechanism. FD-011 lacked a required checkpoint artifact; FD-012 proves ticket prose cannot constrain a contradictory launcher.
* Disposition: fresh construction-capable paste is the immediate compatibility path. The durable launch contract must treat invocation mode as part of the enforced control surface. If a clean construction-capable invocation still exits, classify the in-turn rule itself as failed rather than blaming the launcher again.

#### Duplicate-ID recurrence escalation outcome

The duplicate control-record ID defect recurred at R41: C73 was appended twice with the same ID and identical body after earlier divergent duplicate C67/C68 entries. Under the second-occurrence rule, this was escalated to the user. Decision: fix immediately after the R41 pre-push gate lands and before HAR-6.

Authorized shape for the next unit: minimal idempotency on the existing HAR-34 record, not an event bus. RED artifact first reproduces duplicate append; then one authority or content-addressed allocation, identical retry idempotency, divergent-body same-ID fail-closed, deterministic replay, concurrency/retry fixtures, full gates, one commit, independent exact-SHA review.

### FD-013 - protected root commit omitted from indeterminate-range scan

* Gate: <issue id="ecb76e90-9d07-40b8-b0dd-c97d74899dc4" href="https://linear.app/harneet2512/issue/HAR-57/gt-pipelined-deep-review-record">HAR-57</issue> exact-SHA review of R41 implementation `d0d5136279bbbff43d19e8132ecf19c6607fd244` (parent `fdda310143dd15127040ec42b68cf32adfbf0ec6`).
* Class: `PROTOCOL_CHECKPOINT_OMISSION`; related mechanism: range-boundary exclusion.
* Finding: `.githooks/pre-push::range_has_protected_change(base, local_sha)` enumerates `base..local_sha`. In the no-remote-ancestor fallback, `base` is the repository root, so the root commit is excluded. A repository whose root commit contains a protected path and has no remote ancestor is incorrectly labeled `unprotected_root_fallback` and accepted without any preceding RED receipt.
* File/symbol evidence: `.githooks/pre-push` functions `range_has_protected_change` and the two root-fallback call sites; the shipped fixture covers a protected commit after an unprotected root but not a protected root itself.
* Decisive fixture: fresh exact-SHA detached worktree at `d0d5136279bbbff43d19e8132ecf19c6607fd244`; temporary repository with one root commit containing `gt-index/internal/resolver/resolver.go`, no remote refs; feed a new-branch pre-push row with zero remote SHA. Observed output: `range_source=unprotected_root_fallback`, `HOOK_EXIT=0`, then review assertion `REVIEW_RED: protected root commit was accepted without a RED receipt.` Review fixture exit 1.
* Recurrence: first occurrence of this range-boundary class. It does not reopen FD-011; it shows the prospective enforcement added for FD-011 is incomplete.
* Required repair: add a dedicated failing root-only protected-history fixture first; make root-inclusive inspection explicit for the no-ancestor and non-ancestor fallbacks; retain unprotected root-only pass; rerun focused fixture matrix, plain/tagged Go, diff/format/vendor, LFS compatibility, and exact-SHA review. Do not broaden protected paths or add a framework.
* Disposition: `CHANGES_REQUIRED`; repair not yet authorized by the <issue id="86d56678-c8ae-480d-a918-dc9ce2c320d2" href="https://linear.app/harneet2512/issue/HAR-34/live-chat-codex-and-reviewer-control-thread">HAR-34</issue> fixed header. Exact repair SHA pending.

### FD-013 - hashed RED receipt accepts fabricated execution

* Gate: independent review of R41 implementation SHA `d0d5136279bbbff43d19e8132ecf19c6607fd244`, parent RED boundary `fdda310143dd15127040ec42b68cf32adfbf0ec6`.
* Class: `FABRICATED_EVIDENCE`.
* Finding: `.githooks/pre-push::validate_red_receipt` validates commit subject, dedicated paths, declared nonzero `exit_code`, and hashes of fixture/output bytes, but never executes the declared fixture command. A fixture whose real exit is 0 plus an invented output file and receipt declaring exit 1 is accepted as valid RED evidence.
* Decisive fixture: independent temporary repo committed `fake_red.sh` containing `exit 0`, an invented `fake.out`, and a fully hash-consistent receipt declaring `exit_code=1`; followed by a protected resolver commit. The exact-SHA hook exited 0 and traced `red_fixture=...`, while direct execution of the fixture exited 0.
* Recurrence: same `FABRICATED_EVIDENCE` class as FD-002/FD-009/FD-010 and therefore escalated by the recurrence rule. This gate was intended to prevent self-reported evidence but currently certifies a self-consistent claim without observing execution.
* Disposition: CHANGES REQUIRED. The repair must independently execute the fixture from the immutable fixture commit in an isolated temporary checkout, capture real exit/output, and compare them to the receipt; execution mismatch, output mismatch, path escape, or non-failing fixture fails closed.

### FD-014 - repair authorization contradicted the live hook

* Gate: HAR-34 R42 control-scope validation against groundtruth hook at exact SHA `d0d5136279bbbff43d19e8132ecf19c6607fd244`.
* Class: `PROTOCOL_SPEC_UNSATISFIABLE`; attempt count 1.
* Finding: R42 authorized one protected implementation repair commit directly after `d0d5136279bbbff43d19e8132ecf19c6607fd244`, but the live `.githooks/pre-push::check_range` requires every protected commit's immediate parent to be a dedicated valid `test(red):` fixture commit. The authorized shape could never pass the gate without bypassing or weakening it.
* File and symbol evidence: exact-SHA `.githooks/pre-push::is_protected_path`, `fixture_files_are_dedicated`, `validate_red_receipt`, and `check_range`; `check_range` resolves `fixture_commit=$(git rev-parse "$commit^")` for each protected commit and fails when that parent is not a valid dedicated RED boundary.
* Decisive check: model the R42 graph as `d0d513... -> protected repair`. Its fixture parent is `d0d513...`, whose subject is `fix(hooks): enforce fixture-first protected pushes`, not `test(red): ...`; validation therefore deterministically fails before any repository mutation. C80 independently reached the same result and stopped cleanly.
* Standing structural fix: before writing any future control authorization, validate the proposed exact base, commit graph, commit subjects, touched-path classes, parent relationships, receipt/evidence placement, and push range against the exact live hook bytes at that base. Record the satisfiable witness in the control scope. If no witness exists, refuse to authorize and correct the shape first. This validation must cover all enforced preconditions, not only parent-is-RED.
* Current correction witness: validated at exact base `d0d5136279bbbff43d19e8132ecf19c6607fd244` against live hook blob `689ea9bb0ee50a9cb0da1e92b464a41e31a70372`. R43's graph is `d0d513... -> dedicated RED-only commit -> one protected implementation repair`. RED-only paths are limited to hook tests and RED artifacts, which `is_protected_path` excludes; on the first new-branch push, `d0d513...` is the nearest remote ancestor and the range contains only that unprotected RED boundary. On the second push, the remote base is the RED SHA, the range contains the protected implementation, and its immediate parent is the dedicated `test(red):` boundary carrying fixture, output, and receipt. This satisfies the current topology, path, ancestry, range, evidence-placement, and push-shape preconditions without bypassing or weakening the hook. Runtime receipt verification remains the implementation behavior under repair, not a precondition claimed green in advance.
* Recurrence/escalation: first occurrence. Any second `PROTOCOL_SPEC_UNSATISFIABLE` occurrence stops authorization and escalates to the user with both control scopes and exact hook bytes.
* Disposition: R42 superseded by R43. Permanent pre-authorization satisfiability validation is required prospectively; exact repair SHAs pending.

### FD-015 - construction authorization redispatched as CONTROL-only

* Gate: HAR-34 R43 worker continuation after exact header synchronization at reviewer 43 / worker 43.
* Class: `UNENFORCED_CONTROL_CLAIM`; recurrence of FD-012; attempt count 2.
* Finding: the worker consumed R43 in C81/C82, but the invocation again carried a hard `CONTROL MODE ONLY` boundary and emitted C83 `CONTROL_ONLY_HANDOFF` without repository inspection or mutation. No new groundtruth ref appeared; the last remote boundary remained `d0d5136279bbbff43d19e8132ecf19c6607fd244`.
* Producing mechanism: the installed `%USERPROFILE%\.gt-control\linear-bridge.py` is the dispatch classifier/launcher. HAR-34 R24 records the original defect explicitly: the listener launched CONTROL for every HAR-34 update, so authorized construction could not reach WORK. The bridge is exercised by the resident/fallback path; Scheduled Tasks `GT Resident Agent`, `GT Resident Watchdog`, and `GT-HAR44-Supervisor` keep that installed path alive but are not the prompt source to patch blindly.
* Decisive evidence: C83 states the invocation was explicitly CONTROL-only after R43 was acknowledged and authorization remained live; fresh remote fetch showed no successor of `d0d513...`. This repeats FD-012's exact mechanism after a ticket-only launcher prompt was added, proving the ticket prose was not a producing fix.
* Standing repair: patch the installed bridge/dispatcher on the user's machine so an authorized, unconsumed construction scope launches the HAR-56 construction-capable prompt, while CONTROL remains reserved for unauthorized/malformed/already-consumed events. Inspect installed task actions and source before mutation, preserve rollback, syntax-check, restart only the owning task/process, then prove one authorized delivery yields WORK and one unauthorized delivery yields CONTROL without duplicate writer.
* Escalation: second occurrence. Stop silent retries and surface the local launcher repair to the user.
* Fix location: HAR-44 section `Paste-once repair - FD-015 construction launcher recurrence`.
* Disposition: escalated; local paste-once repair pending user execution and read-back proof.

#### FD-015 execution routing correction

The current Codex child has host write access, so the launcher repair is worker-owned HAR-56 unit 001; no user paste is required. Apply the existing HAR-44 repair content during the healthy current cycle with two extra hard gates: touch neither product repository, and do not stop/restart/replace/signal/modify the live parent/current construction child. If the owning bridge is not proven idle, stage the corrected installed bytes for the next safe restart and record `STAGED_NOT_RESTARTED`. Completion requires identical read-back receipts here and in HAR-44 with exact changed path/function, before/after hashes, backup path, process/task ownership, syntax check, WORK/CONTROL/dedupe probes, and activation state.

Standing class fix: any future host-side gap that the worker can repair with existing host access becomes a numbered HAR-56 unit. Ask the user only after positive evidence that the worker lacks the required capability, credential, permission, physical access, spending/publication approval, or benchmark-design decision.

### FD-016 - nested Git commands inherited the source repository environment

* Gate: first two unpublished R43 implementation push attempts after RED SHA `fb5235c7bf7e304468690d1ac29f872af99beac7`.
* Class: `ISOLATION_BOUNDARY_ESCAPE`; attempt count 2 before structural repair.
* Finding: a Git hook inherits repository-local environment variables. Nested `git -C <temporary-path>` commands therefore continued targeting the source common Git directory. The first attempt moved the source worktree to the fixture SHA; a later `git init` set the shared repository `core.bare=true`. Archive-only materialization avoided that escape but removed `.git`, so repository-aware fixtures failed with `fatal: this operation must be run in a work tree`.
* Decisive evidence: source reflog recorded the unexpected checkout during pre-push; `git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree` became false and `core.bare` read true after the second attempt; both post-commit pushes failed and their remote refs remained absent. The exact auto-push failure log remains under the common Git directory.
* Structural repair: restore and read back `core.bare=false`; before every nested Git command and fixture process, unset the names returned by `git rev-parse --local-env-vars`; initialize an independent repository, disable its hooks, fetch only the exact fixture SHA, detach, then execute. The aggregate fixture now snapshots source HEAD, index tree, and tracked status before/after every hook invocation and fails with exit 99 on mutation.
* Closure evidence: pushed repair `3c43119cee251ca210454a48ffa59bd05cb81b41`; focused matrix exit 0 with source/config unchanged; post-commit pre-push succeeded and remote read-back matched. Exact-SHA review remains pending, so disposition is `REPAIRED_AWAITING_INDEPENDENT_REVIEW`.
* Recurrence rule: any future nested repository operation from a hook must explicitly clear repository-local Git environment and prove source-state immutability; a second occurrence stops hook-based construction until the isolation substrate is redesigned.

### FD-017 - non-executable RED fixture accepted

* Gate: <issue id="ecb76e90-9d07-40b8-b0dd-c97d74899dc4" href="https://linear.app/harneet2512/issue/HAR-57/gt-pipelined-deep-review-record">HAR-57</issue> REV-005 independent exact-SHA review of `3c43119cee251ca210454a48ffa59bd05cb81b41`.
* Class: `EXECUTION_IDENTITY_WEAKENING`; first occurrence.
* Finding: a receipt-bound fixture blob with mode `100644` is accepted and executed through `sh` when its failure/output otherwise match. This violates R42's explicit executable-fixture criterion and allows a receipt to certify bytes Git does not mark executable.
* Mechanism: shared `regular_blob_at` permits `100644|100755` for both fixture and output.
* Decisive fixture/output: `.githooks/tests/nonexec.sh` mode `100644`, actual exit 7, exact output `real failure\n`; hook exit 0 and review assertion exit 1.
* Required structural repair: distinct blob-mode predicates; fixture exactly `100755`; output regular and non-symlink; tracked regression in aggregate matrix; exact-SHA review. Disposition `OPEN_CHANGES_REQUIRED`.
